questions.question_text: For which of these integrals does the reverse chain rule $\int f'(x)\left[f(x)\right]^{n}dx$ apply?

options.why: There is no factor of $x$ at all, so the inner derivative $2x$ is missing.
The factor $x^{2}$ is not a constant multiple of the inner derivative $2x$.
Here the inner derivative is $3x^{2}$, and $8x$ is not a constant multiple of it.

questions.solution_text:
The derivative of the inner function must appear as a factor, up to a constant multiple.
For $f(x) = x^{2} + 7$, $f'(x) = 2x$ and $8x = 4(2x)$.
So the rule applies to $\int 8x\left(x^{2} + 7\right)^{3}dx$.

questions.question_text: In $\int\left(4x^{3} - 10x\right)\left(x^{4} - 5x^{2}\right)^{6}dx$, which choice correctly names $f(x)$ and $f'(x)$ for the reverse chain rule?

options.why: Took the outside factor as the inner function; the inner function is the expression inside the bracket.
Differentiated $-5x^{2}$ as $-5x$ instead of $-10x$.
Took the whole power as the inner function and dropped the inner derivative factor.

questions.solution_text:
The inner function is the expression inside the bracket.
$f(x) = x^{4} - 5x^{2}$
$f'(x) = 4x^{3} - 10x$
